name: Escitalopram
route_note: Oral tablets or solution once daily.
originator: H. Lundbeck A/S, with Forest Laboratories

discovery.note: Lundbeck resolved racemic citalopram and developed the active S-enantiomer as a separate drug as citalopram patents neared expiry.

tagline: Single-enantiomer SSRI derived from citalopram, used for depression and anxiety
summary: Escitalopram is the S-enantiomer of citalopram and one of the most widely used SSRIs. It is approved for major depression and generalised anxiety disorder and, in Europe, for several other anxiety disorders.
mechanism: Escitalopram binds the primary (orthosteric) site of the serotonin transporter with high selectivity and also interacts with an allosteric site that slows its own dissociation, producing potent and sustained reuptake inhibition.
It has negligible affinity for adrenergic, muscarinic, histamine and dopamine receptors. Like citalopram it prolongs the QT interval in a dose-dependent way, though less at equivalent doses.
uses: Panic disorder, social anxiety disorder and OCD (EU labelling)

history.title: Development
history.detail: Lundbeck begins developing the S-enantiomer of citalopram.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Escitalopram is approved in Europe as Cipralex.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Lexapro (Forest) for depression in August 2002.

history.title: GAD
history.detail: Escitalopram is approved in the US for generalised anxiety disorder.

history.title: Adolescents
history.detail: The FDA approves escitalopram for depression in adolescents aged 12–17.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic escitalopram launches in the US.

history.title: Paediatric GAD
history.detail: The FDA extends the GAD indication to children aged 7 and older.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2C19, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 to S-desmethylcitalopram

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Escitalopram is a classic example of a 'chiral switch' from a racemic drug.
